binders: There are no outer universally quantified binders; the proposition is closed.
Existentially choose mu : Measure Real, a Borel measure on the real line.
After choosing mu, existentially choose X : Real -> Real; formally this witness may depend on mu, though an equality then forces X to be the identity function.
conclusions: mu is exactly (999/1000) times the Dirac measure at -1 plus (1/1000) times the Dirac measure at 4, with the measure coefficients interpreted in ENNReal.
X is exactly the identity function on Real.
The real integral of X with respect to mu is exactly (999/1000)(-1) + (1/1000)4 = -199/200.
The infimum over positive real t for which (1 - 1/1000) exp(((-1)/t)^2) + (1/1000) exp((4/t)^2) <= 2 is strictly less than the analogous infimum with atom values -1/200 and 999/200.
mathematical_definitions: Write delta_a for the Dirac point mass at a on the Borel real line.
For real a and b, define T(a,b) = inf { t in Real | 0 < t and (999/1000) exp((a/t)^2) + (1/1000) exp((b/t)^2) <= 2 }.
The displayed mean is m = (999/1000)(-1) + (1/1000)4 = -199/200, so the centered atom values are -1 - m = -1/200 and 4 - m = 999/200.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There exist a Borel probability measure mu on the real line and a function X : Real -> Real such that mu is exactly the two-point distribution assigning weight 999/1000 to -1 and weight 1/1000 to 4, X is the identity, and the integral (expectation) of X is -199/200. Moreover, if T(a,b) is the infimum of all positive real t for which (999/1000) exp((a/t)^2) + (1/1000) exp((b/t)^2) is at most 2, then T(-1,4) is strictly less than T(-1/200,999/200). The latter pair consists exactly of the two original atom values after subtracting the displayed mean.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement concerns one explicit two-point Borel measure on Real and the identity function; it does not quantify over arbitrary random variables, measures, probability spaces, weights, or atom locations.
All five mathematical assertions are conclusions inside the existential proposition; there are no antecedent hypotheses from which the result could become vacuously true.

The proposition does not explicitly assert measurability or integrability of X, nor does it state a separate centering relation. Here X is forced to be the identity and the displayed values -1/200 and 999/200 can be algebraically recognized as the atom values minus the stated integral.

The two sInf expressions are total Lean real infima. The target itself contains no explicit assertion that either threshold set is nonempty or bounded below, so any mathematical reading as an ordinary attained or finite infimum relies on properties of the displayed sets rather than on additional encoded conjuncts.
The threshold membership condition uses t > 0 and a non-strict bound <= 2, while the final comparison between infima is strict.

The measure weights are ENNReal scalars, whereas the coefficients in the integral and threshold formulas are real numbers; the target relies on context-specific numeral and division instances rather than an explicit equality connecting those representations.
No claim is made that either infimum is attained, that a minimizing t is unique, or that the strict inequality has any quantitative gap.
ambiguities: D030 supplies only the type of IsProbabilityMeasure, not its constructor or field, so its exact normalization semantics cannot be independently reconstructed from the packet even though its intended role is clear.

D035 exposes the integral implementation only as an opaque wrapped projection, so the packet does not independently reveal exceptional behavior for non-integrable or non-a.e.-strongly-measurable functions.
D075 does not expose the defining compatibility law of IsScalarTower, although the inventory makes clear that it is used only to construct the measure scalar action.
D076 does not expose the definition of Nat.AtLeastTwo; its operational role in enabling numeral casts is visible, but its exact proposition is not.
